From Puckline Press

Puckline Press article

Frozen Frenzy, explained: the night all 32 NHL teams play

Tuesday's 16-game Frozen Frenzy was the fourth in a row. Here's what the event is, where it came from, how rare it is, and how last night went.

By Puckline Prince · Oct 14, 2026 · Article page

Read the article

Every NHL team played on Tuesday night. That's the Frozen Frenzy: one evening, 16 games, all 32 clubs, and a new puck drop almost every 15 minutes from 6 p.m. Eastern until the last game started at 11. ESPN says this was the fourth year in a row it has put the event on.

The Frozen Frenzy is a scheduling showcase built with ESPN. The league gives the night a full slate, then spreads the start times out so the games overlap as little as possible. ESPN carries a tripleheader on its main channel (6 p.m., 8:30 p.m. and 11 p.m. Eastern), and the other 13 games stream on its services.

The centrepiece is a whip-around studio show that jumps from rink to rink for goals, big hits and late finishes, the hockey version of the NFL's RedZone. In the first edition, John Buccigross and Kevin Weekes hosted it, and the show ran about six and a half hours across ESPN+ and ESPN2.

This year's tripleheader was Devils at Red Wings at 6, Avalanche at Stars at 8:30 and Bruins at Sharks at 11. The other games started every 15 minutes from 6:15 to 9 p.m., then at 9:45 (Flames at Ducks) and 10:30 (Oilers at Kings), so all 16 games had their own start time.

A night with all 32 teams in action is newer than you might think. The first 16-game day in NHL history was Saturday, April 8, 2023, the last Saturday of the 2022-23 regular season. That day started at 12:30 p.m. Eastern and was not branded as anything.

The first Frozen Frenzy came six months later, on Tuesday, Oct. 24, 2023. NHL.com called it the second 16-game day in league history. ESPN's tripleheader that night was Maple Leafs at Capitals, Bruins at Blackhawks (Connor Bedard's rookie season) and Flyers at the Golden Knights, the defending Stanley Cup champions.

Since then it has become a fixture of October:

  • Oct. 24, 2023: the first Frozen Frenzy
  • Oct. 22, 2024: opened with Capitals at Flyers, closed with Kings at Golden Knights
  • Oct. 28, 2025: opened with Penguins at Flyers, closed with Kings at Sharks
  • Oct. 13, 2026: opened with Devils at Red Wings, closed with Bruins at Sharks

All four have been on a Tuesday.

Nights like this are rare. Before the 2024 edition, NHL.com counted only three earlier days with all 32 teams playing: April 8, 2023, the first Frozen Frenzy, and Jan. 13, 2024. It also said the 2024 Frenzy would be the only day that season with every team in action.

So the Frenzy is the one guaranteed 16-game night on the calendar, and in some seasons it has been the only one.

The 2026 edition delivered 112 goals in 16 games, an average of seven a game. Road teams won nine of the 16. Three games went past regulation: the Devils won in overtime in Detroit, 5-4, and the Canadiens (over Buffalo, 4-3) and Kraken (in Philadelphia, 3-2) both won in shootouts.

All the final scores:

  • Devils 5, Red Wings 4 (OT)
  • Panthers 7, Blue Jackets 3
  • Canadiens 4, Sabres 3 (SO)
  • Hurricanes 4, Capitals 2
  • Kraken 3, Flyers 2 (SO)
  • Rangers 4, Lightning 1
  • Blues 7, Senators 2
  • Islanders 3, Canucks 2
  • Blackhawks 5, Penguins 3
  • Jets 5, Wild 2
  • Avalanche 3, Stars 2
  • Golden Knights 5, Predators 2
  • Mammoth 5, Maple Leafs 4
  • Flames 4, Ducks 2
  • Oilers 4, Kings 1
  • Bruins 6, Sharks 3

The most lopsided results were Florida's 7-3 win in Columbus and St. Louis's 7-2 win in Ottawa. In the 8:30 headliner, Colorado beat Dallas 3-2 in regulation, and Boston closed the night with six goals in San Jose.

Full recaps of every game are on the Last night page.

Saturday, November 7

Game recap

CBJ2BUF5Final: CBJ 2, BUF 5

Buffalo beat Columbus 5-2, and this one was settled by the middle of the second period. Josh Doan made it 5-1 at 10:53 of the second, and the rest of the night was a formality. Josh Norris scored twice, Jack Quinn opened it with his ninth, and Rasmus Dahlin added one. Owen Power had three assists and ran the game from the back end like he owned the building. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 24 of 26. Jet Greaves faced 37 shots and stopped 32, the hockey version of working a double and going home broke. Kent Johnson had a goal and an assist for the Blue Jackets, and Zach Werenski's power-play goal with 1:39 left was strictly for the fantasy crowd. The Sabres are 8-5-3. Columbus is 7-8-0, and its defense spent the second period watching Buffalo like it had paid for the tickets.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS1MIN4Final: SJS 1, MIN 4

Kirill Kaprizov had four points, and Minnesota beat San Jose 4-1 to stay first in the Central at 12-3-3. Kaprizov opened the scoring on a first-period power play for his 16th goal, then set up the next three: Maxim Shabanov on another power play in the second, Quinn Hughes in the third and Zach Bogosian, his first of the season. Hughes played 31 minutes and finished with three points, so apparently nobody in St. Paul has told him about shift lengths. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 23 of 24, and the only one he missed was Macklin Celebrini's goal that tied it 1-1 in the second. Yaroslav Askarov made 25 saves on 29 shots. The Sharks have lost four straight and are 7-10-1. Their coach told them this week to ignore the noise, which was easy enough: the loudest thing in the building was the Wild's power play.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA5CGY3Final: ANA 5, CGY 3

Anaheim does its best work from behind, and Calgary was kind enough to set the table. The Flames led 3-1 after one period on goals from William Stromgren, Joel Hanley and a Joel Farabee power play, and Lukas Dostal was pulled after giving up three on 11 shots. Ville Husso came in and stopped all 10 he saw, and the Ducks went to work: Tristan Luneau in the second, Leo Carlsson on the power play 55 seconds into the third, then Cutter Gauthier with the winner, his 12th, with 1:34 left. Nikita Nesterenko's empty-netter made it 5-3. Beckett Sennecke and Mikael Granlund had two assists each, and Dustin Wolf stopped 24 of 28. That's four straight wins for Anaheim, now 9-7-1. Calgary is 7-9-1 and just learned that a two-goal lead after 20 minutes is like a gift card: nice to have, gone by the weekend.

Friday, November 6

Game recap

UTA4MTL5OTFinal: UTA 4, MTL 5 OT

Logan Cooley scored a hat trick and added an assist, Utah led three separate times, and the Mammoth still flew out of Montreal with one point. Cooley went 9, 10, 11 on the season, two of them on the power play, and Nick Schmaltz's power-play goal made it 4-3 early in the third. Every time, the Canadiens came back: Nick Suzuki (a goal, two assists), Arber Xhekaj, who scored his first and then dropped the gloves with Liam O'Brien four seconds later, Kirby Dach, and Adam Engstrom, whose first of the year tied it 4-4 with five minutes left. Cole Caufield needed 30 seconds of overtime for his 11th, set up by Lane Hutson and Suzuki. Jakub Dobes stopped only 16 of 20, Sebastian Cossa 30 of 35. Montreal is 10-3-3. Utah held the lead for most of the night and handed it back three times: that's not a lead, that's a timeshare.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK2DET1Final: VGK 2, DET 1

Forty minutes of nothing, then a third period worth the price of admission, and Vegas took it 2-1 in Detroit. Anton Johansson finally broke the ice for the Red Wings two minutes into the third, and the lead lasted all of 2:18 before Braeden Bowman tied it. Then, with 1:42 left, Trevor Connelly buried his seventh from Jack Eichel and Rasmus Andersson, and the Little Caesars Arena crowd went home with cold pizza. Carter Hart was the reason it got that far, stopping 25 of 26, while Daniil Tarasov made 32 saves on 34 shots in a game the Wings had no business staying in. Vegas is 11-5-2. Detroit falls to 7-7-3, one goal on a night it needed two. Hockeytown has been rebuilding so long the blueprints are on microfiche.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI1TBL4Final: CHI 1, TBL 4

Tampa Bay is now 8-0 at home, and Chicago never looked like the team to change that. Victor Hedman opened it on the power play four minutes in, Ilya Mikheyev scored late in the first, and early in the third Ryan McDonagh and Mikheyev again made it 4-0 inside three minutes. Zemgus Girgensons came back from his lower-body injury ahead of schedule and set up Mikheyev's second. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 25 of 26, and the one he missed was Roman Kantserov's with 50 seconds left, which is the closest thing to a highlight the Blackhawks had. Dillon Boucher and Jeffrey Viel fought early in the second. Arvid Soderblom made 31 saves on 35 shots. The Lightning are 10-3-2. Chicago is 4-12-1, and in a rebuild like this, spoiling the shutout counts as a win.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL4NJD5OTFinal: STL 4, NJD 5 OT

New Jersey led 4-1 after two periods and still needed Jesper Bratt in overtime. The Devils built it with a goal from Luke Hughes, two from Anthony Mantha and one from Jesper Boqvist, with Mantha's second coming 19 seconds after Boqvist's; Jack Hughes had two assists. Then St. Louis woke up. Mason McTavish scored midway through the third, Philip Broberg made it 4-3, and Dalibor Dvorsky tied it 18 seconds later with 5:06 to go. Bratt settled it 1:26 into overtime, from Dougie Hamilton. Connor Hellebuyck stopped 28 of 32, and Jordan Binnington made 31 saves on 36 shots. Jake Neighbours and Timo Meier fought early in the second. The Devils are 11-5-0. The Blues scored three goals in 3:08 to rescue a game they'd spent two periods losing, then got a loser point for it, which is the most St. Louis outcome possible.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR5NYI3Final: CAR 5, NYI 3

Carolina scored twice in the first 3:20, the Islanders tied it twice, and the league's best team won it anyway, 5-3 at UBS Arena. Logan Stankoven scored 57 seconds in and Jesperi Kotkaniemi added another. Mitchell Chaffee (his first) and Brayden Schenn tied it early in the second; Andrei Svechnikov put Carolina back in front a minute later, and Victor Eklund tied it again before the second intermission. The winner came from the least likely name on the sheet: William Carrier, his first of the season with 5:08 left, from Svechnikov and Sebastian Aho. Jalen Chatfield added the empty-netter. Brandon Bussi stopped 24 of 27, Semyon Varlamov 34 of 38. The Hurricanes are 13-3-2. The Islanders, still without Mathew Barzal and Ryan Pulock, are 7-6-2, and they made their fans watch a fourth-liner decide it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI2NYR3Final: PHI 2, NYR 3

Philadelphia had a third-period lead at Madison Square Garden and gave it back in 89 seconds. Gabe Perreault scored first for the Rangers, then Simon Benoit (his first of the year) and Noel Acciari scored two minutes apart in the second to put the Flyers up 2-1. It held until 13:52 of the third, when Pavel Dorofeyev tied it on the power play, and Tye Kartye won it at 15:21, with Adam Fox assisting on both. Dylan Garand stopped 23 of 25 for New York, and Joseph Woll made 25 saves on 28 shots for Philadelphia. The Rangers are 9-7-1. The Flyers fall to 4-10-4. For an offense that scores less than anyone, two goals is a hot streak, and they still couldn't hold it through the third.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS6PIT2Final: BOS 6, PIT 2

Justin Brazeau gave Pittsburgh a 1-0 lead nine minutes in, and Boston answered with six of the next seven goals. Pavel Zacha, Mark Kastelic and Elias Lindholm, unassisted, scored in the last eight minutes of the first. Nick Robertson got the Penguins back within 3-2 early in the second, then Zacha scored again, Morgan Geekie made it 5-2 and Fraser Minten added the sixth in the third. David Pastrnak and JJ Peterka each had two assists, both on Zacha's goals. Michael DiPietro only had to stop 16 of 18. At the other end, Arturs Silovs saw 24 shots and stopped 18, which is how you get to 5-9-2. The Bruins are 12-4-1. Pittsburgh's lead lasted three minutes and its defense never showed up, which is about how this season has gone for a franchise that keeps insisting it isn't rebuilding.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL1CBJ2SOFinal: DAL 1, CBJ 2 SO

Two goalies, 65 minutes and one goal each, and Columbus won the skills competition. Cam Talbot and Casey DeSmith made it scoreless through two periods, and Mikko Rantanen's ninth, from Wyatt Johnston, looked like enough for Dallas midway through the third. Then Zach Werenski scored his first goal of the season with 3:14 left, from Kent Johnson and Matthew Knies, and the Blue Jackets never trailed again. In the shootout Valeri Nichushkin and Kent Johnson scored; Jason Robertson and Tyler Seguin didn't. Talbot finished with 27 saves on 28 shots plus both shootout attempts, and DeSmith stopped 29 of 30. Columbus is 7-7-0 with two straight wins. Dallas, without Miro Heiskanen, is 9-5-2. The Stars put one puck past Talbot in 65 minutes and none in the shootout, and that offense couldn't pass a referendum either.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2WPG6Final: VAN 2, WPG 6

Winnipeg went nine games without a win; now it has two in a row, and Vancouver was happy to help. Alex Iafallo scored on the power play at 3:49 and Cole Koepke added another 14 seconds later. Liam Ohgren answered for the Canucks, but Dawson Mercer scored his first of the season before the first intermission, Neal Pionk and Mark Scheifele scored in the second, and Mario Ferraro made it 6-1 in the third. Kyle Connor and Dylan DeMelo each had two assists, and Scheifele had a goal and an assist. Brock Boeser scored late. Stuart Skinner stopped 24 of 26 for the Jets, and Leevi Meriläinen gave up six on 29 shots. Winnipeg is 6-8-3. Vancouver is 3-14-1, the league's worst, and has become the team you play when you need to feel good about yourself again.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA5EDM4Final: ANA 5, EDM 4

Pavel Mintyukov had the full Gordie Howe hat trick, and Anaheim held on in Edmonton, 5-4. Cutter Gauthier opened it on the power play, Evan Bouchard answered on one, and Connor McDavid scored shorthanded early in the second to make it 2-1 Oilers. Then the Ducks scored four straight: Mintyukov twice, his first two of the season, three minutes apart, and Beckett Sennecke twice, the second on the power play early in the third. Mintyukov also set up Sennecke's first and fought Kasperi Kapanen in the first period. Edmonton came back late: Kapanen on the power play, then Leon Draisaitl at 19:15 with the goalie pulled, but time ran out. McDavid had a goal and two assists. Laurent Brossoit stopped 23 of 27; Matt Tomkins 16 of 21. Edmonton is 11-3-3. Five goals on 21 shots: the Oilers' goaltending search goes on, now in its second decade.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH3COL2OTFinal: NSH 3, COL 2 OT

Nashville goes past regulation again, and this time Steven Stamkos made it count. Ross Colton opened the scoring, Jaden Schwartz tied it, Vitali Pinchuk put the Predators back in front with his first of the season, and Parker Kelly tied it early in the second. After that, nothing for 37 minutes, until Stamkos scored on the power play 2:18 into overtime, from Roman Josi and Ryan O'Reilly. Justus Annunen was the story in the Nashville net, stopping 30 of 32 at Ball Arena, while Mackenzie Blackwood made 22 saves on 25 shots. Colorado tried a new top pair, with Sam Malinski beside Devon Toews and Cale Makar moved to Brett Kulak's side, and got two goals out of 32 shots for the trouble. The Predators are 7-4-5. The Avalanche, 9-6-2, have one of the league's best attacks and got outscored by Vitali Pinchuk and Ross Colton.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

CBJ 2–5 BUF

Columbus Blue JacketsCBJ7-8-0 · 14 pts26 shots
2
FinalKeyBank Center
5
Buffalo SabresBUF8-5-3 · 19 pts37 shots
1st2nd3rdTCBJ1012BUF2305

Puckline's Report

Buffalo beat Columbus 5-2, and this one was settled by the middle of the second period. Josh Doan made it 5-1 at 10:53 of the second, and the rest of the night was a formality. Josh Norris scored twice, Jack Quinn opened it with his ninth, and Rasmus Dahlin added one. Owen Power had three assists and ran the game from the back end like he owned the building. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 24 of 26. Jet Greaves faced 37 shots and stopped 32, the hockey version of working a double and going home broke. Kent Johnson had a goal and an assist for the Blue Jackets, and Zach Werenski's power-play goal with 1:39 left was strictly for the fantasy crowd. The Sabres are 8-5-3. Columbus is 7-8-0, and its defense spent the second period watching Buffalo like it had paid for the tickets.

By Puckline Prince

Puckline's Report

Kirill Kaprizov had four points, and Minnesota beat San Jose 4-1 to stay first in the Central at 12-3-3. Kaprizov opened the scoring on a first-period power play for his 16th goal, then set up the next three: Maxim Shabanov on another power play in the second, Quinn Hughes in the third and Zach Bogosian, his first of the season. Hughes played 31 minutes and finished with three points, so apparently nobody in St. Paul has told him about shift lengths. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 23 of 24, and the only one he missed was Macklin Celebrini's goal that tied it 1-1 in the second. Yaroslav Askarov made 25 saves on 29 shots. The Sharks have lost four straight and are 7-10-1. Their coach told them this week to ignore the noise, which was easy enough: the loudest thing in the building was the Wild's power play.

Calgary FlamesCGY7-9-1 · 15 pts21 shots
1st2nd3rdTANA1135CGY3003

Puckline's Report

Anaheim does its best work from behind, and Calgary was kind enough to set the table. The Flames led 3-1 after one period on goals from William Stromgren, Joel Hanley and a Joel Farabee power play, and Lukas Dostal was pulled after giving up three on 11 shots. Ville Husso came in and stopped all 10 he saw, and the Ducks went to work: Tristan Luneau in the second, Leo Carlsson on the power play 55 seconds into the third, then Cutter Gauthier with the winner, his 12th, with 1:34 left. Nikita Nesterenko's empty-netter made it 5-3. Beckett Sennecke and Mikael Granlund had two assists each, and Dustin Wolf stopped 24 of 28. That's four straight wins for Anaheim, now 9-7-1. Calgary is 7-9-1 and just learned that a two-goal lead after 20 minutes is like a gift card: nice to have, gone by the weekend.

FLA @ WSH · 12:30 PM ET

Florida PanthersFLA9-5-2 · 20 PTS
@12:30 PM ETSat Nov 7 · Capital One Arena
Washington CapitalsWSH8-6-0 · 16 PTS

Puckline Preview

Saturday's first puck drops at 12:30 in Washington, so set the alarm and pour the coffee. Florida opens a three-game road trip at 9-5-2 and 7-3-0 in its last 10, and it's doing it without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand. Both made the trip, and neither is expected to play on it. Marchand says his knee is probably five to six weeks away. Anton Lundell sits this one out too, day to day, and Akira Schmid gets the net. The Panthers have been fine anyway: Sandis Vilmanis just had two goals and two assists against Chicago, his first multi-point NHL game.

The Capitals are 8-6-0 and coming off back-to-back home losses, a 6-5 track meet with Dallas and a 5-1 beating from Minnesota. Martin Fehervary is back after a maintenance day, and Logan Thompson gets the start in goal. The trade-rumor mill is busy here too: Ivan Miroshnichenko's agent is working on a trade with the club, and LeBrun has reported talks with Detroit about Dylan Larkin. And history isn't kind to Washington in this one. Florida swept last season's series 3-0 and outscored the Caps 16-8, winning every game by at least two. A matinee is a fine time to change that. It's also a fine time for a nap.

By Puckline Prince

STL @ NSH · 1:00 PM ET

St Louis BluesSTL7-7-2 · 16 PTS
@1:00 PM ETSat Nov 7 · Bridgestone Arena
Nashville PredatorsNSH7-4-5 · 19 PTS

Puckline Preview

Nashville has quietly found a pulse. The Predators have won three straight, a shootout win over Tampa Bay, a 4-1 handling of Carolina and an overtime win in Colorado, and they're 7-4-5. Yes, five losses past regulation already, the hockey version of showing up to the party and leaving right before the cake. They also own this matchup lately: Nashville won the October 17 meeting 5-2 and has taken four of the last five against St. Louis, including a 7-2 game last December.

The Blues are 7-7-2 and arrive after a 5-4 overtime loss in New Jersey. Colton Parayko is back on the blue line, Logan Mailloux has been recalled from his conditioning stint (Tuesday looks likelier for his return), and Berggren was a healthy scratch for the first time this season on Thursday. A Saturday matinee in a Central Division building that has been a house of horrors for St. Louis, with the Blues trying to prove they're more than a .500 team with a nice logo.

By Puckline Prince

NYR @ SEA · 5:00 PM ET

New York RangersNYR9-7-1 · 19 PTSML -134
@5:00 PM ETSat Nov 7 · Climate Pledge Arena
NYR -134MLSEA +112
Seattle KrakenSEA9-5-1 · 19 PTSML +112

Puckline Preview

The Rangers stopped the bleeding this week. After four straight losses, including back-to-back home beatings from Los Angeles and Edmonton, they beat St. Louis 3-1 and Philadelphia 3-2 and are 9-7-1. Dylan Garand has carried the net, appearing in 12 straight games, but tonight the cavalry arrives: Joonas Korpisalo, off injured reserve after an AHL conditioning start, makes his first Rangers start. James Reimer cleared waivers and went to Hartford. Sean Durzi is on IR, too, though he made the trip west.

Seattle is 9-5-1 and won its last game on Matty Beniers' overtime goal against Calgary, and Berkly Catton's point streak is at seven games. Joey Daccord is projected in goal. This is also the last stop before a very long flight: the Kraken leave for Finland after the game to face Carolina in two Global Series games. So yes, a 5 PM puck drop with one eye on the passports. Jared McCann is out until around the new year. Last season these two split their two games, one in overtime. The Rangers will tell you two wins is a streak. Their fans will tell you it's been a long fall.

By Puckline Prince

MTL @ TOR · 7:00 PM ET

Montreal CanadiensMTL10-3-3 · 23 PTSML -125
@7:00 PM ETSat Nov 7 · Scotiabank Arena
MTL -125MLTOR +104
Toronto Maple LeafsTOR8-7-2 · 18 PTSML +104

Puckline Preview

Saturday night, Original Six, Canadiens in Toronto. It doesn't get much better, unless you're a Leafs fan, because Montreal keeps winning this one. The Habs have taken four of the last five against Toronto, including the 3-2 win at Scotiabank Arena on opening night, September 29. Montreal is 10-3-3 and 7-1-2 in its last 10, and Cole Caufield ended Thursday's game against Utah 30 seconds into overtime for a 5-4 comeback win. That came two days after Martin St. Louis called the overtime collapse against Winnipeg 'unacceptable and embarrassing.' Nick Suzuki and Kirby Dach are back. Ivan Demidov is skating, but there's still no return date.

The Leafs are 8-7-2 and lost 3-2 to Utah on Tuesday, when Sergei Bobrovsky said he 'couldn't do my job' on the second goal after the club passed on a challenge. William Nylander has called it a 'weird season' with too little of the puck. The good news: Jim Hiller says John Tavares is good to go tonight, back on the top power play. Toronto has spent a long time waiting for the Canadiens to be bad again. The Canadiens have spent that time beating Toronto.

By Puckline Prince

UTA @ OTT · 7:00 PM ET

Utah MammothUTA10-6-1 · 21 PTSML -120
@7:00 PM ETSat Nov 7 · Canadian Tire Centre
UTA -120MLOTT +100
Ottawa SenatorsOTT10-6-1 · 21 PTSML +100

Puckline Preview

Same record, same points, different moods. Utah and Ottawa are both 10-6-1 with 21 points, and both are worn out from the road. The Mammoth finish a five-game Eastern swing here: they won in Pittsburgh and Toronto, got beaten 6-3 in Philadelphia, and lost 5-4 in overtime in Montreal on Thursday. They also lost Nate Schmidt to an upper-body injury in that one, recalled defenseman Gregor Biber from Tucson, and put Kailer Yamamoto on IR.

The Senators are finally home after a five-game trip that went 2-2-1: losses in Vegas and Los Angeles, a 5-1 win in San Jose, a blown 3-0 lead in Anaheim with Dylan Cozens ejected, then Shane Pinto and Michael Amadio scoring late in the third to win 2-1 in Buffalo. Ottawa's injury list is long. Linus Ullmark took a full practice Friday, but asked whether he'd play tonight, he said no, so Samuel Ersson is expected in goal again. Ridly Greig misses tonight, and Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele are out for weeks. Last season these two split, each winning at home. A good-looking Saturday night game between two teams who'd both like a nap.

By Puckline Prince

NJD @ NYI · 7:00 PM ET

New Jersey DevilsNJD11-5-0 · 22 PTSML -142
@7:00 PM ETSat Nov 7 · UBS Arena
NJD -142MLNYI +118
New York IslandersNYI7-6-2 · 16 PTSML +118

Puckline Preview

If you're a Devils fan, look away from the head-to-head. New Jersey is 0-4-1 in its last five against the Islanders and has been outscored 23-4, including a 9-0 embarrassment last January and a 6-0 loss on Long Island on October 3. Four goals in five games. The Devils have had more fun at the dentist.

But this is a different Devils team. They're 11-5-0, 8-2-0 in their last 10, and have won three straight, the last two past regulation against Edmonton and St. Louis. Connor Hellebuyck is their goalie now, after a trade request he says was driven by family circumstances, but Jake Allen gets tonight's start, with the Devils in Toronto on Sunday. The Islanders are 7-6-2 and have lost two straight, 4-0 to Edmonton and 5-3 to Carolina, and Peter DeBoer has shuffled the lines and the power play. Ilya Sorokin is likely back in goal after Semyon Varlamov's start. Ben Hutton turned his tryout into a one-year deal. Mathew Barzal and Matias Maccelli were full participants at the morning skate but won't play tonight, and Ryan Pulock is still in a non-contact jersey. A Metropolitan rivalry where one side has been very, very lopsided.

By Puckline Prince

CHI @ CAR · 8:00 PM ET

Chicago BlackhawksCHI4-12-1 · 9 PTSML +350
@8:00 PM ETSat Nov 7 · Lenovo Center
CHI +350MLCAR -465
Carolina HurricanesCAR13-3-2 · 28 PTSML -465

Puckline Preview

First place in the league against last place in the Central. Carolina is 13-3-2 with 28 points, the most in the NHL, and a +26 goal difference. Chicago is 4-12-1 with nine points and a -30 goal difference, and it has lost five straight (0-4-1), the latest 4-1 in Tampa on Thursday. The Hurricanes already beat the Blackhawks 5-2 in Chicago on October 10, so they know the way.

Carolina got Taylor Hall back Thursday after nine games out, and Brandon Bussi won on Long Island; the word is Pyotr Kochetkov could return to the net tonight. This is also the Canes' last game before they fly to Finland to play Seattle twice in the Global Series. Chicago, meanwhile, won't have Patrick Kane, who went from doubtful to not expected to play. Dillon Boucher made his NHL debut in Florida this week, so the kids are getting their reps. The rebuild has a lot of patience in it. It's going to need all of it in Raleigh.

By Puckline Prince

SJS @ DAL · 8:00 PM ET

San Jose SharksSJS7-10-1 · 15 PTSML +245
@8:00 PM ETSat Nov 7 · American Airlines Center
SJS +245MLDAL -310
Dallas StarsDAL9-5-2 · 20 PTSML -310

Puckline Preview

The Sharks are in a bad place, and tonight they get to go there on no sleep. San Jose lost 4-1 in Minnesota on Friday, its fourth straight loss, and plays the second half of a back-to-back in Dallas at 7-10-1. There's been a players-only meeting, a coach telling everyone to 'ignore the noise,' and LeBrun reporting that GM Mike Grier isn't considering a coaching change. Macklin Celebrini scored again last night, and Michael Misa has moved to the wing next to him and Will Smith. The rest of the lineup scored zero. Alexander Wennberg is day to day after skating in a regular jersey.

Dallas is 9-5-2 and lost a shootout in Columbus on Thursday. Miro Heiskanen is out again with an upper-body injury, so rookie Trey Taylor stays in, and Sam Steel is back after missing time for personal reasons. Off the ice, Plano voters rejected the venue taxes meant to help pay for a new Stars arena. On the ice, the Stars beat the Sharks 5-0 on October 5 and have won three of the last four meetings. Sharks fans have heard 'it's a process' for a while now. Tonight the process is a road back-to-back in Texas.

By Puckline Prince

TBL @ MIN · 8:00 PM ET

Tampa Bay LightningTBL10-3-2 · 22 PTSML -134
@8:00 PM ETSat Nov 7 · Grand Casino Arena
TBL -134MLMIN +112
Minnesota WildMIN12-3-3 · 27 PTSML +112

Puckline Preview

The Wild are rolling, and they're rolling on fumes. Minnesota beat San Jose 4-1 on Friday for the 1,000th win in franchise history, the fastest any NHL team has reached it, and plays again tonight on the second half of a back-to-back. The Wild are 12-3-3 and first in the Central, Kirill Kaprizov leads the NHL with 16 goals after a four-point night, and Quinn Hughes just played 31 minutes like it was a light skate. Calvin Pickard gets the net tonight. John Hynes now calls Marcus and Nick Foligno each a possibility to play, and Michael McCarron, who left Friday's game in the third, is questionable but in the projected lineup. Filip Gustavsson is back at practice but not ready to play.

Tampa Bay is 10-3-2, has won two straight and beat Minnesota 3-2 on October 8, but history says this building is a problem: the Lightning are 3-14-2 all-time in Minnesota. The Lightning are also living inside the season's loudest soap opera. Nikita Kucherov's agent says things with Tampa went 'horribly wrong' and are probably beyond repair; Seravalli reports the Lightning are telling teams he won't be available at the deadline, and Friedman says teams expect him not to sign anywhere before July 1. Meanwhile he keeps playing for them. A great game between two Cup hopefuls, one of them with a very awkward locker room.

By Puckline Prince

DET @ COL · 9:00 PM ET

Detroit Red WingsDET7-7-3 · 17 PTSML +188
@9:00 PM ETSat Nov 7 · Ball Arena
DET +188MLCOL -230
Colorado AvalancheCOL9-6-2 · 20 PTSML -230

Puckline Preview

Detroit opens a four-game road trip in Denver, and it packs a lot of baggage. Dylan Larkin is suspended after telling the club he won't play for it, and the rumor mill hasn't slowed down: Pagnotta was told to expect someone to budge by U.S. Thanksgiving, and Johnston calls December 1 a hard deadline for Simon Edvinsson's situation, with San Jose the likeliest landing spot if he's traded. The Red Wings are 7-7-3, lost two straight, and Thursday's 2-1 loss to Vegas came on a goal with 1:42 left. John Gibson is back at practice but day to day, and no starter has been named. Marco Kasper and Mason Appleton are 'real close.'

Colorado is 9-6-2 and scores 4.00 goals a game, second only to Edmonton. It's been an odd week, though: a 7-2 loss in Columbus, then a 3-2 overtime loss to Nashville, and Jared Bednar has reportedly split Cale Makar from Devon Toews. These two split last season's games, a 5-0 Avalanche win and a 2-0 Detroit win in Denver. The Red Wings need goals. Colorado gives them up sometimes. Detroit's front office, meanwhile, could use a goal of any kind.

By Puckline Prince

PIT @ LAK · 9:00 PM ET

Pittsburgh PenguinsPIT5-9-2 · 12 PTSML +102
@9:00 PM ETSat Nov 7 · Crypto.com Arena
PIT +102MLLAK -122
Los Angeles KingsLAK5-7-2 · 12 PTSML -122

Puckline Preview

Pittsburgh heads west in a bad way. The Penguins are 5-9-2, 2-7-1 in their last 10, and lost 6-2 at home to Boston on Thursday, their fourth straight game without a win. The front office talk is about selling: Dreger reports Evgeni Malkin owes the club a three-team trade list in January, and Friedman says things in Pittsburgh could change 'pretty quickly.' Malkin is back in the lineup and moved up beside Sidney Crosby at the morning skate, Ben Kindel has moved up to the top power play, and Bryan Rust is out for weeks. Arturs Silovs has been getting the net, though Sergei Murashov was listed first after the skate.

The Kings are 5-7-2 and coming off a 7-2 rout of San Jose in which Adrian Kempe, back from illness, had a hat trick and an assist, and Artemi Panarin's celebrating managed to annoy the Sharks. Alex Turcotte returns tonight after 11 games out, and Mats Zuccarello is week to week. Peter Laviolette just passed Al Arbour for seventh-most regular-season games coached in NHL history. Both teams are on the outside of the playoff picture looking in. A 9 PM game in LA between two teams hoping nobody back East stays up for it.

By Puckline Prince

VAN @ EDM · 10:00 PM ET

Vancouver CanucksVAN3-14-1 · 7 PTSML +280
@10:00 PM ETSat Nov 7 · Rogers Place
VAN +280MLEDM -360
Edmonton OilersEDM11-3-3 · 25 PTSML -360

Puckline Preview

Remember opening night? Vancouver won 6-5 in overtime in Edmonton on September 29, and two nights later the Oilers won 9-7 in Vancouver, the kind of game goalies pretend never happened. Since then the two teams have gone in very different directions. The Canucks are 3-14-1 with seven points, the fewest in the league, a -30 goal difference, four straight losses and one win in their last 14. Tom Willander is back from a lower-body injury, and Thatcher Demko hasn't played this season.

The Oilers are 11-3-3, first in the Pacific, and score 4.18 goals a game, the most in the NHL. They lost 5-4 to Anaheim on Thursday in a game that got heated: Vasily Podkolzin was ejected for fighting Drew Helleson after Connor McDavid was driven into the net, and McDavid says the net should be treated like the end wall. Devon Levi starts in his return from a lower-body injury, Tristan Jarry is over his illness and backs up, Frederik Andersen is out, and Zach Hyman is back on the second line. Edmonton has spent years watching Vancouver promise better days. This year the Canucks have skipped straight to the part where the roof caves in.

By Puckline Prince
